title: Seat mapping
intro: Which switch port each seat is on. The IP and MAC are read off that port from the switches' MAC tables, so you only type one in for a seat whose port isn't known yet. Ports come from the cables and from check-ins; what you enter here wins over them. Only accounts with seat access see it: this is personal data.
searchPlaceholder: Seat, switch, port, nick, IP, MAC…
onlyOffPlan: Only seats not on the plan
countSplit: {{count}} seats: {{onPlan}} on the plan, {{off}} not on any plan
offPlanHint: No seat block on any hall has this seat. It comes from a seat source only.
empty: No seat has a mapping yet.
removeQuestion: Remove the hand entry for seat {{seat}}? The other sources show again.
importHelp: Columns: seat, switch, port, ip, mac, nick, note (the first line names them; leave out the ones you don't have). Every row is checked first; if one is wrong, nothing is imported.
replace: Replace all hand entries (seats not in the file lose theirs)
hintsHelp: Only needed while the seat's port isn't known: Floorbit reads both off the port.
findHelp: Plug the machine in, type its MAC, and Floorbit looks up the port it is on. You can change it again later.
found: Found on {{switch}} {{port}}. Save to keep it.
foundHeld: Found on {{switch}} {{port}}, but that port is seat {{seat}} now. Free it there first.
resolve_one: Find the port for {{count}} entry with only an IP or MAC
resolve_other: Find the ports for {{count}} entries with only an IP or MAC
resolved: {{found}} got their port, {{missed}} not seen on the network, {{taken}} on a port another seat has.
